body.x: Marketon Inc. (CEO Richard Yang) participated in CES 2024, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition held in Las Vegas from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday) local time.

As a technology company in the display field, Marketon is strengthening its business in the hologram display sector, focusing on providing more natural images compared to AR (Augmented Reality) and VR (Virtual Reality) amid the industry’s shift from high definition to immersive displays.

In particular, Marketon has overcome the limitations of holograms, which traditionally had limited usability in bright environments due to high ambient light. They have secured hologram technology that allows clear content representation even in well-lit spaces, showcasing distinctive technological capabilities.

Marketon aims to expand the application of this technology to various fields, including the metaverse, medical displays, and automotive control systems. They are intensifying research and development efforts to supply their technology more widely.

Marketon showcased its completed lineup of hovering hologram products at this year’s CES due to its efforts to advance hologram technology. The distinctive feature lies in the refinement of hologram technology, maximizing the versatility of both the technology and the products. It supports image representation and interaction, creating the illusion of images floating in the air without being constrained by location or environment.

Additionally, it incorporates facial recognition and tracking features, offering users the optimal viewing angle for interacting with content. These features enable the implementation of interactive images in the air, allowing for a wide range of applications such as AI assistants, automated vending systems (kiosks), and remote video calls.

body.cap: Marketon unveiled part of its hovering hologram display product line at CES 2024 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: With its distinctive hologram technology, Marketon has been recognized as an outstanding innovative company, earning a ‘Hi Seoul Enterprise’ certification from the Small Business Administration (SBA). The company also attracted significant attention from numerous global attendees at the exhibition venue.

Richard Yang, the founder of Marketon, said, “Amid a somewhat stagnant development in technologies like AR and VR in the metaverse field, our hovering hologram product line is a differentiated device targeting the needs of potential customers.” He added, “Having made thorough preparations, we received positive responses from numerous visitors at the CES 2024 venue.”

He continued, “In particular, to discuss the potential usage scenarios of our product, various international buyers and investors from the United States, Dubai, Singapore, and more visited our booth during the exhibition period. As a result, we now have a more positive outlook on the possibility of leading the global premium content market.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global innovative technology trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion is being operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. The Seoul Pavilion, which has collaborated with 13 institutions, is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish itself as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Participating institutions include SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
